messages.content: give me a sentence with ride about going to the park.
i ride to the park with my sister.
now make it yesterday.
i rode to the park with my sister yesterday.
what if i want a question using did?
did you ride to the park with your sister yesterday?
why ride after did instead of rode?
did goes with ride in that question. rode works in the simple past sentence without did.
now say we are doing it now.
my sister and i are riding to the park now.
can you know what kind of vehicle we use?
no. ride does not give a specific vehicle in these sentences.
only give the yesterday sentence again.
i rode to the park with my sister yesterday.
write a longer story about a child asking how to find a room inside a school. the person helping should ask what place the child already knows before giving the way there.

a child wanted to find a room where a reading group would meet. he asked a worker near the door. the worker began giving places inside the school, but the child did not know any of them yet. then the worker asked whether he had seen the library. he had been there that morning, so they used it as the start. from the library, the reading room was through the next door on the right. the child said that short part back and went to look. he found the room and came back to say thank you before the group began. the building had not changed, but the explanation worked better when it began from a place he knew.
why did the first explanation not help much?
it used places the child did not know.
what place could they use as a start?
the library, where he had been that morning.
write the useful way there as a short request.
from the library, go through the next door on the right.
why was that not a full map of the school?
he did not need the whole map for this task. he needed the part from a known place to the room.
finish with the child ready for reading.
he put his book on the table in the right room and sat down before the group started.
my friend showed me a drawing of a tree. i like the shape. help me say that without making up the story behind the drawing.
i like the shape of the tree in your drawing.
can i ask how they made it?
yes. you could say: i like the shape of the tree. how did you start drawing it?
why not say it is about when they were a child?
because you do not know that from the shape. you can ask about the story behind it without choosing that story for them.
only give the question about the story behind it.
is there a story behind this drawing?
what if they say no, they just wanted to draw a tree?
then you can like the shape without asking for another reason. the drawing can be useful to them just as a drawing.
make that explanation shorter.
you can like the shape without asking for a story behind it.
only give the first sentence again.
i like the shape of the tree in your drawing.
if i say i am too tired to read now, does that mean i can never read?
no. it is about being tired now, not about whether you can read at all.
make a sentence that leaves tomorrow open.
i am too tired to read now, but i may read tomorrow.
can i know tomorrow will be better?
not for sure. you have not said how you will feel tomorrow. may keeps that open.
make that explanation shorter.
may does not give a sure answer about tomorrow.
now make it about a long story instead of any reading.
i am too tired for a long story now.
does that rule out one short sentence?
not by itself. you may still want to read a short sentence.
make that explanation shorter.
a short sentence may still be possible.
only give the first now sentence again.
i am too tired to read now.
write a longer story about a child changing a story because she enjoys making up something new, then saying clearly which part is new. do not make her changed part a fact about the original book.

a child read a story where a person left a book at home. she wanted to make up what would happen if the person took it on the journey instead. she told her brother the new start, and he asked why he did not remember that part from the book. she explained that she was making another story, not telling him the original again. they put the two ideas on different pages. one page kept what the book said, and the other began with her change. now they could talk about the new story without saying those were the words in the book. changing a made up story was part of their game, while knowing what the book said was a different task.
what did she change?
she made the person take the book on the journey instead of leaving it at home.
why did her brother ask about it?
he did not remember that part from the original book.
give the important difference in one sentence.
she kept what the book said on one page and her new idea on another.
what should she say before telling her new part?
this is my changed story, not what happened in the original book.
finish with them choosing what happens after the new start.
they read the changed page together and chose what might happen next in their own story.
i finished reading three pages and looked at two more without reading them. how many pages did i finish reading?
three pages.
how many pages did i look at in all?
five, if the three you read and the two more are different pages.
why not say i read five?
because looking at a page is not always reading it. you said you did not read the two more.
now i read one of those two.
then you have finished reading four pages, and one of the looked at pages is still not read.
can you know how much i understood?
no. the number of pages does not tell us your understanding of them.
only give how many pages i have not read from that group.
one page.
if i read the same first page again, does that make all five finished?
no. reading one again does not finish the page you have not read yet.
is the book itself is useful the same as the boy himself is useful?
no. itself is about the book, and himself is about the boy. the words go with different things.
make that explanation shorter.
itself is about the book. himself is about the boy.
can i say the book opened itself in a made up story?
yes, in a made up story. that gives the idea that no person opened it in that story.
can i say that about a real book without seeing what happened?
you should not say you know that. you may only know the book is open, not how it opened.
now make a sentence where the boy opened the book himself.
the boy opened the book himself.
why not itself at the end of that sentence?
because himself is about the boy doing it. itself would point to the book instead.
use words without point.
himself is about the boy. itself is about the book.
only give the boy sentence again.
the boy opened the book himself.
write a longer story about a child and her aunt talking about a mother. the child should ask which mother is in the story. use no real name.

a child and her aunt looked at an old photo. the aunt began telling a story about her mother visiting the house. the child first thought the story was about her own mother, because that was the mother she knew best. after hearing another detail, she asked whose mother was in the story. the aunt explained that she was talking about her own mother, who was the grandmother of the child. they looked at the picture again and used grandmother for a while to keep it clear. the person in the photo had not changed. the family word had changed with the person telling the story. once the child understood, the shorter word her could be used without the same problem.
why did the child need to ask?
she and her aunt could use mother for different people.
who was the aunt talking about?
her own mother, who was the grandmother of the child.
make the important idea more simple.
they used grandmother so the child knew which person the aunt was talking about.
what question could the child ask?
do you mean my mother or your mother?
finish with the story clear enough to go on.
the aunt told the next part using grandmother, and the child could follow who was visiting the house.
i first asked if a book was good. now i think i should ask if it is good for what i want to learn.
that makes the question more specific. what do you want to learn from it?
make that answer shorter.
what do you want to learn from the book?
i want to learn basic words with simple examples.
then ask whether it has simple examples that help with the words you want to learn, instead of only asking whether someone likes it.
make that explanation shorter.
ask for the detail that helps with your learning goal.
write my question.
does this book have simple examples for learning basic words?
does a yes mean it is the best book for everyone?
no. it answers one question about what you need, not every possible use of the book.
only give my question again.
does this book have simple examples for learning basic words?
i am going to the market after lunch. i want to ask my friend if they would like to come, without saying they already said yes.
i am going to the market after lunch. would you like to come with me?
can i make it clear i am still going if they cannot?
yes. you can add: i will go either way, but you are welcome to join.
use no either in the new sentence.
i plan to go even if you cannot come, but i would like you to join if you want to.
make that message shorter.
i plan to go even if you cannot come. would you like to join me?
why not say we are going?
it would sound like both of you have chosen. only you have given a plan so far.
make that explanation shorter.
we would sound like both had chosen, but only you have.
only give the first message asking my friend to come again.
i am going to the market after lunch. would you like to come with me?
write a longer story about someone asking why a picture moved and getting only where it is. the place answer should be useful but not the whole answer.

a child asked why her picture was no longer on the door. her father said it was on the shelf. she went to look and found it there, but still wanted to know why it had moved. she returned and explained that she was not asking only where to find it. her father said the door had needed cleaning and he had put the picture away from the water. now she knew both the place and the reason. she asked if they could put it back after the door was ready. he said yes, and they chose a place where it would be easy to see. asking the reason again had not made the first answer wrong. it had added the part she still needed.
what did the first answer give?
it gave the new place of the picture.
what question was still open?
why the picture had been moved.
give that difference in one sentence.
the place answer helped her find the picture, but did not give the reason for moving it.
what could she say to ask again in a kind way?
thank you. i found it. could you tell me why it was moved?
finish with the picture back after cleaning.
when the door was clean, they put the picture back together and stood where they could both see it.
my friend said yes to reading one page with me. give me a short thank you without asking for the whole book.
thank you. one page together will help.
can you make it shorter?
thank you for helping.
does that ask for another page?
no. it thanks them without changing the request.
only say goodbye now.
goodbye.
